angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 466,815 km at 77.83 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.8491 +/- 0.0234 mas (same row, RUWE 1.38): 77.83 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.671 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Lillo-Box et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-969 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A.109L/abstract): 466,815 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.734 +/- 0.014 solar masses from Lillo-Box et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-969 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A.109L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4435 +/- 80 K from Lillo-Box et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-969 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A.109L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lillo-Box et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-969 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A.109L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-969.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.650, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
